name: Wisconsin Youth Conservation Congress
org: Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources with the Wisconsin Conservation Congress
what_you_do: Join a youth group tied to Wisconsin's citizen conservation panel. You get a mentor. You volunteer with DNR staff, such as on fish and wildlife surveys. You learn how natural resource policy is made.
who_can_apply: Wisconsin students interested in the outdoors. It is best suited to high school students and younger students may apply. Some DNR volunteer tasks are only for ages 16 and up. You can take part through the summer after senior year.
pay_detail: No pay. Free to join, apart from your own travel costs.
duration: Year-round. Two district meetings plus Spring Hearings and a May convention, with extra field days.
deadline_text: No deadline. The FAQ says applications are accepted and reviewed on an ongoing basis.
how_to_apply: Fill out the YCC application and parent consent form from the DNR YCC page. Or contact the YCC Coordinator, Kyle Zenz, at kyle.zenz@wisconsin.gov or 715-299-0925.
notes: Volunteer program, not a job. A parent or guardian must sign the consent form. It can count toward school service-learning or independent study credit if your school agrees. The packet's example activities are from 2025, so check this year's schedule.
